name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_STATEMENT_BASED_Q06 - Mechanical advantage conditions and principle of moments in levers

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: An ideal lever operates on the principle of moments, which requires load arm \(\times\) load \(=\) effort arm \(\times\) effort for rotational equilibrium.

Statement II: An ideal lever has a mechanical advantage strictly greater than one when its effort arm is shorter than its load arm.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक आदर्श उत्तोलक आघूर्णों के सिद्धांत पर कार्य करता है, जिसके घूर्णन संतुलन के लिए भार भुजा \(\times\) भार \(=\) आयास भुजा \(\times\) आयास होना आवश्यक है।

कथन II: एक आदर्श उत्तोलक का यांत्रिक लाभ स्पष्ट रूप से एक से अधिक होता है जब उसकी आयास भुजा उसकी भार भुजा से छोटी होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Rotational Equilibrium of a Lever
For an ideal light lever pivoted at the fulcrum, mechanical equilibrium requires the algebraic sum of external torques about the fulcrum to be zero: \(\sum \tau = 0\).
This yields \(d_1 F_1 = d_2 F_2\), where \(F_1\) is the load, \(d_1\) is the load arm, \(F_2\) is the effort, and \(d_2\) is the effort arm. This is the principle of moments: load arm \(\times\) load \(=\) effort arm \(\times\) effort. Hence, the first statement is correct.

Step 2: Definition and Condition for Mechanical Advantage
Mechanical Advantage (M.A.) is defined as the ratio of load to effort: \(\text{M.A.} = \frac{F_1}{F_2} = \frac{d_2}{d_1} = \frac{\text{effort arm}}{\text{load arm}}\).
For \(\text{M.A.} > 1\), the ratio \(\frac{d_2}{d_1}\) must be greater than one, which means that the effort arm \(d_2\) must be strictly longer than the load arm \(d_1\). If the effort arm were shorter than the load arm (\(d_2 < d_1\)), the mechanical advantage would be less than one. Hence, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1: उत्तोलक का आघूर्ण सिद्धांत
आलंब के परितः घूर्णन संतुलन के लिए कुल बाह्य आघूर्ण शून्य होना चाहिए: \(d_1 F_1 = d_2 F_2\)। इसका अर्थ है: भार भुजा \(\times\) भार \(=\) आयास भुजा \(\times\) आयास। इसलिए प्रथम कथन सही है।

चरण 2: यांत्रिक लाभ की शर्त का मूल्यांकन
यांत्रिक लाभ (M.A.) \(\frac{\text{भार}}{\\text{आयास}} = \frac{\text{आयास भुजा}}{\text{भार भुजा}} = \frac{d_2}{d_1}\) होता है।
यांत्रिक लाभ एक से अधिक होने के लिए आयास भुजा \(d_2\) को भार भुजा \(d_1\) से बड़ा होना चाहिए (\(d_2 > d_1\))। जब आयास भुजा छोटी होती है, तो यांत्रिक लाभ एक से कम हो जाता है। इसलिए द्वितीय कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I सही है लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_STATEMENT_BASED_Q07 - Angular momentum vector alignment and vector product reflection invariance

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For an arbitrary rigid body without reflection symmetry rotating about a fixed axis, the total angular momentum vector \(\mathbf{L}\) is always parallel to the angular velocity vector \(\boldsymbol{\omega}\).

Statement II: Under coordinate reflection through the origin (\(\mathbf{r} \to -\mathbf{r}\)), the cross product \(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}\) of two polar vectors does not change sign.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: बिना परावर्तन सममिति वाले किसी यादृच्छिक दृढ़ पिंड के लिए जो एक स्थिर अक्ष के परितः घूर्णन कर रहा है, कुल कोणीय संवेग सदिश \(\mathbf{L}\) सदैव कोणीय वेग सदिश \(\boldsymbol{\omega}\) के समानांतर होता है।

कथन II: मूलबिंदु के माध्यम से निर्देशांक परावर्तन (\(\mathbf{r} \to -\mathbf{r}\)) के तहत, दो ध्रुवीय सदिशों का सदिश गुणनफल \(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}\) अपना चिह्न नहीं बदलता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Angular Momentum Vector Components in Fixed Axis Rotation
For a rigid body rotating with angular velocity \(\boldsymbol{\omega} = \omega \mathbf{\hat{k}}\), the total angular momentum is \(\mathbf{L} = \mathbf{L}_z + \mathbf{L}_\perp\), where \(\mathbf{L}_z = I_{zz} \omega \mathbf{\hat{k}}\) and the transverse components are \(L_x = -I_{xz}\omega\) and \(L_y = -I_{yz}\omega\).

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
Unless the rotation axis is an axis of symmetry or a principal axis of inertia, the off-diagonal mass moments \(I_{xz}\) and \(I_{yz}\) do not vanish. Consequently, \(\mathbf{L}_\perp \neq \mathbf{0}\), and the total angular momentum \(\mathbf{L}\) is not parallel to the rotation axis \(\boldsymbol{\omega}\). Hence, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Parity Reflection Behavior of the Vector Cross Product
Under space reflection, every coordinate vector changes sign: \(\mathbf{a} \to -\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{b} \to -\mathbf{b}\).
The cross product transforms as: \((-\mathbf{a}) \times (-\mathbf{b}) = (-1)^2 (\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}) = \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}\).
Because the minus signs cancel in pairs, the cross product retains its exact sign and direction under space inversion, behaving as an axial vector (pseudovector). Hence, the second statement is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

Final Conceptual Answer: The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

चरण 1: स्थिर अक्ष घूर्णन में कोणीय संवेग सदिश घटक
\(z\)-अक्ष के परितः घूर्णन कर रहे पिंड के लिए कुल कोणीय संवेग \(\mathbf{L} = \mathbf{L}_z + \mathbf{L}_\perp\) होता है, जहाँ \(L_x = -I_{xz}\omega\) तथा \(L_y = -I_{yz}\omega\) अनुप्रस्थ घटक हैं।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
यदि अक्ष सममिति अक्ष नहीं है, तो अनुप्रस्थ घटक शून्य नहीं होते, जिसके कारण कुल कोणीय संवेग \(\mathbf{L}\) कोणीय वेग \(\boldsymbol{\omega}\) के समानांतर नहीं होता है। इसलिए प्रथम कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: सदिश गुणनफल का दिक्-परावर्तन व्यवहार
दिक्-परावर्तन के तहत स्थिति सदिश \(\mathbf{a} \to -\mathbf{a}\) तथा \(\mathbf{b} \to -\mathbf{b}\) में बदल जाते हैं।
इनका सदिश गुणनफल \((-\mathbf{a}) \times (-\mathbf{b}) = \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}\) रहता है, अर्थात् इसका चिह्न नहीं बदलता है। इसलिए द्वितीय कथन सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I गलत है लेकिन कथन II सही है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_STATEMENT_BASED_Q08 - Work energy theorem in fixed axis rotation and rate of kinetic energy change

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The work done by a net external torque \(\tau\) in rotating a rigid body about a fixed axis through an infinitesimal angular displacement \(d\theta\) is given by \(dW = \tau \, d\theta\).

Statement II: For a rigid body with constant moment of inertia rotating about a fixed axis, the instantaneous power delivered by the torque equals the rate of increase of its rotational kinetic energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक स्थिर अक्ष के परितः किसी दृढ़ पिंड को एक अत्यंत सूक्ष्म कोणीय विस्थापन \(d\theta\) से घुमाने में कुल बाह्य बल-आघूर्ण \(\tau\) द्वारा किया गया कार्य \(dW = \tau \, d\theta\) होता है।

कथन II: स्थिर जड़त्व आघूर्ण वाले दृढ़ पिंड के लिए जो एक स्थिर अक्ष के परितः घूर्णन कर रहा है, बल-आघूर्ण द्वारा प्रदान की गई तात्कालिक शक्ति उसकी घूर्णन गतिज ऊर्जा की वृद्धि दर के बराबर होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Work Done by a Torque in Fixed Axis Rotation
For any particle at perpendicular distance \(r_i\) from the fixed axis, the displacement along its circular arc is \(ds_i = r_i \, d\theta\). The work done by the tangential force is \(dW_i = F_{i\perp} ds_i = (F_{i\perp} r_i) d\theta = \tau_i \, d\theta\). Summing over all particles gives \(dW = \sum \tau_i \, d\theta = \tau \, d\theta\), where \(\tau\) is the net torque along the rotation axis. Hence, the first statement is correct.

Step 2: Instantaneous Power and Rate of Change of Rotational Kinetic Energy
Dividing \(dW = \tau \, d\theta\) by \(dt\) gives the instantaneous power: \(P = \frac{dW}{dt} = \tau \frac{d\theta}{dt} = \tau \omega\).
The rotational kinetic energy of the rigid body is \(K = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2\). Differentiating with respect to time for a constant moment of inertia \(I\):
\(\frac{dK}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{1}{2} I \omega^2\right) = I \omega \frac{d\omega}{dt} = I \omega \alpha\).
Applying the dynamic rotational relation \(\tau = I \alpha\), we find:
\(\frac{dK}{dt} = (I \alpha) \omega = \tau \omega = P\).
Thus, the instantaneous power delivered by the external torque is equal to the time rate of increase of rotational kinetic energy. Hence, the second statement is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both the first statement and the second statement are correct.

चरण 1: स्थिर अक्ष घूर्णन में बल-आघूर्ण द्वारा किया गया कार्य
अक्ष से \(r_i\) दूरी पर स्थित कण का चाप विस्थापन \(ds_i = r_i \, d\theta\) होता है, जिससे किया गया कार्य \(dW_i = \tau_i \, d\theta\) प्राप्त होता है। सभी कणों के लिए योग करने पर कुल कार्य \(dW = \tau \, d\theta\) प्राप्त होता है। इसलिए प्रथम कथन सही है।

चरण 2: तात्कालिक शक्ति और गतिज ऊर्जा की वृद्धि दर
तात्कालिक शक्ति \(P = \frac{dW}{dt} = \tau \omega\) होती है।
घूर्णन गतिज ऊर्जा \(K = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2\) का समय के सापेक्ष अवकलन करने पर: \(\frac{dK}{dt} = I \omega \alpha\) प्राप्त होता है।
चूँकि \(\tau = I \alpha\) होता है, अतः \(\frac{dK}{dt} = \tau \omega = P\) प्राप्त होता है। अर्थात् शक्ति गतिज ऊर्जा की वृद्धि दर के बराबर होती है। इसलिए द्वितीय कथन सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I और कथन II दोनों सही हैं।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: Both the first statement and the second statement are correct.

answer.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS11_CH06_STATEMENT_Q01 - Center of mass of symmetric bodies and systems

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The centre of mass of a system of particles can lie at a geometric point where no physical mass of the body is present.

Statement II: For a system composed of two point masses having identical masses, the centre of mass lies at the exact midpoint of the straight line joining them.

Statement III: In the absence of any external force, mutual internal forces between the particles of a system can accelerate the centre of mass.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: कणों के किसी निकाय का द्रव्यमान केंद्र ऐसे ज्यामितीय बिंदु पर स्थित हो सकता है जहाँ निकाय का कोई भौतिक द्रव्यमान उपस्थित न हो।

कथन II: समान द्रव्यमान वाले दो बिंदु कणों से बने निकाय के लिए, द्रव्यमान केंद्र उन्हें मिलाने वाली सरल रेखा के ठीक मध्य बिंदु पर स्थित होता है।

कथन III: किसी बाह्य बल की अनुपस्थिति में, निकाय के कणों के बीच लगने वाले पारस्परिक आंतरिक बल द्रव्यमान केंद्र को त्वरित कर सकते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
English Solution:

Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Centre of Mass Location
The position vector of the centre of mass of a system of \(n\) particles is defined by: \[\vec{R}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\sum m_i \vec{r}_i}{\sum m_i}\] For a continuous mass distribution, this is represented by an integral over the volume. The position of the centre of mass depends strictly on the spatial distribution of mass. In hollow or symmetric structures, such as a uniform thin ring or a hollow sphere, symmetry dictates that the centre of mass lies at the geometric centre, a point in empty space where no material particles exist. Hence, the first statement is true.

Step 2: Two Equal Masses Analysis
Consider two point particles, each of mass \(m\), situated along a coordinate axis at coordinates \(x_1 = 0\) and \(x_2 = d\). The position coordinate of the centre of mass is: \[X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m(0) + m(d)}{m + m} = \frac{m d}{2m} = \frac{d}{2}\] Thus, the centre of mass is positioned precisely midway between the two identical masses. Hence, the second statement is true.

Step 3: Internal Forces and Motion of Centre of Mass
According to Newton's second law for a system of particles, the equation of motion for the centre of mass is: \[\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = M \vec{A}_{\text{cm}}\] By Newton's third law, internal forces between any pair of particles within the system are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. Consequently, the vector sum of all internal forces identically vanishes: \[\sum \vec{F}_{\text{int}} = 0\] Therefore, internal forces can never accelerate the centre of mass of a system. When \(\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = 0\), the acceleration of the centre of mass is strictly zero (\(\vec{A}_{\text{cm}} = 0\)). Hence, the third statement is false.

Step 4: Check and Conclusion
The first statement and the second statement are true, whereas the third statement is false.
Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I and Statement II only.

हिंदी हल:

चरण 1: द्रव्यमान केंद्र की स्थिति का वैचारिक सिद्धांत
\(n\) कणों के निकाय के द्रव्यमान केंद्र का स्थिति सदिश निम्न प्रकार परिभाषित होता है: \[\vec{R}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\sum m_i \vec{r}_i}{\sum m_i}\] द्रव्यमान केंद्र की स्थिति पूरी तरह से द्रव्यमान के स्थानिक वितरण पर निर्भर करती है। सममित या खोखली संरचनाओं जैसे कि एकसमान पतले छल्ले अथवा खोखले गोले में सममिति के कारण द्रव्यमान केंद्र ज्यामितीय केंद्र पर स्थित होता है, जो कि एक रिक्त स्थान है जहाँ कोई भौतिक द्रव्यमान उपस्थित नहीं होता। अतः, प्रथम कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: दो समान द्रव्यमानों का विश्लेषण
समान द्रव्यमान \(m\) वाले दो बिंदु कणों पर विचार कीजिए जो \(x_1 = 0\) और \(x_2 = d\) पर स्थित हैं। द्रव्यमान केंद्र का निर्देशांक निम्न है: \[X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m(0) + m(d)}{m + m} = \frac{d}{2}\] अतः, द्रव्यमान केंद्र दोनों कणों को मिलाने वाली रेखा के ठीक मध्य बिंदु पर स्थित होता है। अतः, द्वितीय कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: आंतरिक बल तथा द्रव्यमान केंद्र की गति
कणों के निकाय के लिए न्यूटन के द्वितीय नियमानुसार: \[\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = M \vec{A}_{\text{cm}}\] न्यूटन के तृतीय नियम के अनुसार, निकाय के कणों के बीच लगने वाले पारस्परिक आंतरिक बल परिमाण में समान और दिशा में विपरीत होते हैं। अतः समस्त आंतरिक बलों का सदिश योग शून्य होता है: \[\sum \vec{F}_{\text{int}} = 0\] इसलिए, आंतरिक बल कभी भी द्रव्यमान केंद्र को त्वरित नहीं कर सकते। यदि \(\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = 0\) हो, तो द्रव्यमान केंद्र का त्वरण अनिवार्य रूप से शून्य होता है। अतः, तृतीय कथन असत्य है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
प्रथम कथन और द्वितीय कथन सत्य हैं, जबकि तृतीय कथन असत्य है।
अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: केवल कथन I और कथन II।

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS11_CH06_STATEMENT_Q02 - Mechanical equilibrium and couple properties of rigid bodies

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: A rigid body is in translational equilibrium if the vector sum of all external forces acting on it is equal to zero.

Statement II: A couple acting on a rigid body produces rotational acceleration without causing any translational acceleration of its centre of mass.

Statement III: If the net external force acting on a rigid body is zero, the total external torque acting on the body has the same value irrespective of the choice of reference origin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक दृढ़ पिंड स्थानांतरणीय संतुलन में होता है यदि उस पर लगने वाले समस्त बाह्य बलों का सदिश योग शून्य हो।

कथन II: किसी दृढ़ पिंड पर कार्य करने वाला बलयुग्म उसके द्रव्यमान केंद्र को कोई स्थानांतरणीय त्वरण दिए बिना घूर्णी त्वरण उत्पन्न करता है।

कथन III: यदि किसी दृढ़ पिंड पर कार्यरत कुल बाह्य बल शून्य हो, तो पिंड पर लगने वाले कुल बाह्य बल आघूर्ण का मान संदर्भ मूल बिंदु के चयन पर निर्भर नहीं करता।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
English Solution:

Step 1: Condition for Translational Equilibrium
A rigid body is in translational equilibrium when its linear momentum remains constant over time. According to Newton's second law for an extended body: \[\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \frac{d\vec{P}}{dt} = M \vec{A}_{\text{cm}}\] When the vector sum of all external forces is zero (\(\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = 0\)), the acceleration of the centre of mass is zero (\(\vec{A}_{\text{cm}} = 0\)), satisfying the condition of translational equilibrium. Hence, the first statement is true.

Step 2: Dynamics of a Couple
A couple consists of a pair of equal and opposite forces acting along parallel, non-collinear lines of action: \[\vec{F}_1 = \vec{F}, \quad \vec{F}_2 = -\vec{F}\] The resultant translational force is: \[\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = \vec{F}_1 + \vec{F}_2 = \vec{F} - \vec{F} = 0\] Because \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = 0\), the linear acceleration of the centre of mass is zero (\(\vec{A}_{\text{cm}} = 0\)). However, because their lines of action are separated by a perpendicular arm \(d\), the torque about any axis perpendicular to the plane of forces is non-zero: \[\tau = F d \neq 0\] This net torque produces rotational acceleration (\(\alpha = \tau / I\)). Hence, the second statement is true.

Step 3: Invariance of Torque when Net Force is Zero
Let the total external torque about an origin \(O\) be: \[\vec{\tau}_O = \sum \vec{r}_i \times \vec{F}_i\] If the origin is shifted to a new point \(O'\) whose position vector relative to \(O\) is \(\vec{r}_0\), the position vector of each particle relative to \(O'\) is \(\vec{r}_i' = \vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_0\). The new net torque about \(O'\) is: \[\vec{\tau}_{O'} = \sum (\vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_0) \times \vec{F}_i = \sum (\vec{r}_i \times \vec{F}_i) - \vec{r}_0 \times \left(\sum \vec{F}_i\right) = \vec{\tau}_O - \vec{r}_0 \times \vec{F}_{\text{net}}\] Given that the net external force is zero (\(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = 0\)), the second term vanishes completely: \[\vec{\tau}_{O'} = \vec{\tau}_O\] Thus, the total torque is independent of the choice of reference point. Hence, the third statement is true.

Step 4: Check and Conclusion
All three statements—the first statement, the second statement, and the third statement—are true.
Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III.

हिंदी हल:

चरण 1: स्थानांतरणीय संतुलन की शर्त
एक दृढ़ पिंड स्थानांतरणीय संतुलन में तब होता है जब उसका कुल रैखिक संवेग नियत रहता है: \[\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = M \vec{A}_{\text{cm}}\] यदि सभी बाह्य बलों का सदिश योग शून्य हो (\(\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = 0\)), तो द्रव्यमान केंद्र का त्वरण शून्य होता है। अतः, प्रथम कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: बलयुग्म की गतिशीलता
एक बलयुग्म दो समान और विपरीत बलों से बना होता है जिनकी क्रिया रेखाएँ समानांतर परंतु असंरेखीय होती हैं: \[\vec{F}_1 = \vec{F}, \quad \vec{F}_2 = -\vec{F}\] कुल बाह्य बल: \[\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = \vec{F} + (-\vec{F}) = 0\] अतः द्रव्यमान केंद्र का स्थानांतरणीय त्वरण शून्य होता है (\(\vec{A}_{\text{cm}} = 0\))। चूँकि दोनों बलों की क्रिया रेखाओं के बीच लंबवत दूरी \(d\) होती है, अतः कुल बल आघूर्ण \(\tau = F d \neq 0\) होता है, जो घूर्णी त्वरण उत्पन्न करता है। अतः, द्वितीय कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: कुल बल शून्य होने पर बल आघूर्ण की स्वतंत्रता
मूल बिंदु \(O\) के परितः कुल बल आघूर्ण: \[\vec{\tau}_O = \sum \vec{r}_i \times \vec{F}_i\] नए बिंदु \(O'\) (जिसका स्थिति सदिश \(\vec{r}_0\) है) के परितः बल आघूर्ण: \[\vec{\tau}_{O'} = \sum (\vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_0) \times \vec{F}_i = \vec{\tau}_O - \vec{r}_0 \times \left(\sum \vec{F}_i\right)\] चूँकि कुल बल शून्य है (\(\sum \vec{F}_i = 0\)): \[\vec{\tau}_{O'} = \vec{\tau}_O\] अतः कुल बल आघूर्ण संदर्भ बिंदु के चयन से स्वतंत्र होता है। अतः, तृतीय कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
तीनों कथन—प्रथम कथन, द्वितीय कथन तथा तृतीय कथन—सत्य हैं।
अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: कथन I, कथन II और कथन III।

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS11_CH06_STATEMENT_Q03 - Moment of inertia and radius of gyration

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The moment of inertia of a uniform solid cylinder of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\) about its standard longitudinal axis of symmetry is \(\frac{1}{2} M R^2\).

Statement II: The radius of gyration \(k\) of a uniform thin rod of length \(L\) about an axis perpendicular to the rod passing through its midpoint is \(\frac{L}{\sqrt{12}}\).

Statement III: The moment of inertia of a body about a given rotational axis depends solely on its total mass and is completely independent of the spatial distribution of mass about that axis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: \(M\) द्रव्यमान और \(R\) त्रिज्या वाले एकसमान ठोस बेलन का उसकी मानक ज्यामितीय अनुदैर्ध्य सममिति अक्ष के परितः जड़त्व आघूर्ण \(\frac{1}{2} M R^2\) होता है।

कथन II: \(L\) लंबाई की एकसमान पतली छड़ का उसके मध्य बिंदु से गुजरने वाली तथा छड़ के लंबवत अक्ष के परितः घूर्णन त्रिज्या \(k\) का मान \(\frac{L}{\sqrt{12}}\) होता है।

कथन III: किसी दिए गए घूर्णन अक्ष के परितः किसी पिंड का जड़त्व आघूर्ण केवल उसके कुल द्रव्यमान पर निर्भर करता है और उस अक्ष के चारों ओर द्रव्यमान के स्थानिक वितरण से पूर्णतः स्वतंत्र होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
English Solution:

Step 1: Moment of Inertia of a Solid Cylinder
A uniform solid cylinder of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\) can be considered as a collection of thin coaxial cylindrical shells of radius \(r\), thickness \(dr\), and length \(H\). The mass of each shell is: \[dm = \rho (2\pi r dr H) = \frac{M}{\pi R^2 H} (2\pi r H dr) = \frac{2M}{R^2} r dr\] Integrating the moment of inertia element \(dI = dm\, r^2\) from \(r = 0\) to \(r = R\): \[I = \int_0^R \frac{2M}{R^2} r^3 dr = \frac{2M}{R^2} \left[\frac{R^4}{4}\right] = \frac{1}{2} M R^2\] This matches the standard result for a solid cylinder about its central longitudinal axis. Hence, the first statement is true.

Step 2: Radius of Gyration of a Uniform Thin Rod
The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod of mass \(M\) and length \(L\) about an axis perpendicular to the rod passing through its centre of mass is: \[I = \frac{1}{12} M L^2\] By definition, the radius of gyration \(k\) relates to the moment of inertia through the formula \(I = M k^2\). Equating the two expressions: \[M k^2 = \frac{1}{12} M L^2 \implies k^2 = \frac{L^2}{12} \implies k = \frac{L}{\sqrt{12}}\] Hence, the second statement is true.

Step 3: Factors Influencing Moment of Inertia
The moment of inertia of a rigid body about an axis is given by: \[I = \sum m_i r_i^2 \quad \text{or} \quad I = \int r^2 dm\] where \(r_i\) is the perpendicular distance of each mass element from the rotation axis. The value of \(I\) explicitly depends on: 1. The total mass \(M\) of the body. 2. The shape and geometric dimensions of the body. 3. The spatial distribution of mass relative to the axis (i.e., mass elements farther from the axis contribute disproportionately more due to the \(r^2\) term). 4. The location and orientation of the rotational axis. Therefore, the moment of inertia is strictly dependent on the mass distribution and is not governed solely by total mass. Hence, the third statement is false.

Step 4: Check and Conclusion
The first statement and the second statement are true, while the third statement is false.
Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I and Statement II only.

हिंदी हल:

चरण 1: ठोस बेलन का जड़त्व आघूर्ण
\(M\) द्रव्यमान और \(R\) त्रिज्या वाले एकसमान ठोस बेलन का उसकी केंद्रीय सममिति अक्ष के परितः जड़त्व आघूर्ण ज्ञात करने के लिए इसे संकेंद्रीय बेलनाकार कोशों में विभाजित किया जा सकता है: \[dI = dm\, r^2\] समाकलन करने पर: \[I = \int_0^R \frac{2M}{R^2} r^3 dr = \frac{1}{2} M R^2\] अतः, प्रथम कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: पतली छड़ की घूर्णन त्रिज्या
लंबाई \(L\) तथा द्रव्यमान \(M\) की एकसमान पतली छड़ का उसके केंद्र से गुजरने वाली तथा लंबाई के लंबवत अक्ष के परितः जड़त्व आघूर्ण: \[I = \frac{1}{12} M L^2\] घूर्णन त्रिज्या \(k\) की परिभाषा से, \(I = M k^2\): \[M k^2 = \frac{1}{12} M L^2 \implies k = \frac{L}{\sqrt{12}}\] अतः, द्वितीय कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: जड़त्व आघूर्ण को प्रभावित करने वाले कारक
घूर्णन अक्ष के परितः जड़त्व आघूर्ण का सूत्र निम्न है: \[I = \sum m_i r_i^2\] जहाँ \(r_i\) घूर्णन अक्ष से प्रत्येक कण की लंबवत दूरी है। जड़त्व आघूर्ण केवल कुल द्रव्यमान पर ही नहीं, बल्कि अक्ष के चारों ओर द्रव्यमान के वितरण, पिंड के आकार तथा अक्ष की स्थिति व अभिविन्यास पर भी सीधे निर्भर करता है। अतः, तृतीय कथन असत्य है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
प्रथम कथन और द्वितीय कथन सत्य हैं, जबकि तृतीय कथन असत्य है।
अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: केवल कथन I और कथन II।

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS11_CH06_STATEMENT_Q04 - Fixed axis dynamics and conservation of angular momentum

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: For a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis, the total angular momentum vector is always parallel to the angular velocity vector, even if the rotational axis is not an axis of symmetry of the body.

Statement II: When a person sitting on a rotating swivel chair with outstretched hands suddenly pulls their hands inward, their moment of inertia decreases and their rotational speed increases in accordance with the law of conservation of angular momentum.

Statement III: For rotation of a rigid body about a fixed axis, the instantaneous power delivered by the net external torque equals the time rate of change of rotational kinetic energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक स्थिर अक्ष के परितः घूर्णन कर रहे दृढ़ पिंड के लिए, कुल कोणीय संवेग सदिश सदैव कोणीय वेग सदिश के समानांतर होता है, भले ही घूर्णन अक्ष पिंड की सममिति अक्ष न हो।

कथन II: जब घूर्णन कर रही किसी घूमने वाली कुर्सी पर अपनी भुजाओं को फैलाकर बैठा व्यक्ति अचानक अपनी भुजाओं को भीतर की ओर सिकोड़ लेता है, तो कोणीय संवेग संरक्षण के नियमानुसार उसका जड़त्व आघूर्ण घट जाता है और उसकी घूर्णन चाल बढ़ जाती है।

कथन III: एक स्थिर अक्ष के परितः दृढ़ पिंड के घूर्णन के लिए, कुल बाह्य बल आघूर्ण द्वारा दी गई तात्कालिक शक्ति घूर्णी गतिज ऊर्जा के समय के साथ परिवर्तन की दर के बराबर होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
English Solution:

Step 1: Alignment of Angular Momentum and Angular Velocity
The total angular momentum of a rotating rigid body is: \[\vec{L} = \sum m_i (\vec{r}_i \times \vec{v}_i) = \sum m_i (\vec{r}_i \times (\vec{\omega} \times \vec{r}_i))\] The vector \(\vec{L}\) has a component \(L_z = I_z \omega\) along the fixed rotation axis \(z\), but it can also possess non-zero components perpendicular to the axis (\(L_x\) and \(L_y\)) unless the rotation axis coincides with a principal axis of symmetry. For an asymmetric body rotating about an arbitrary fixed axis, the perpendicular components \(\vec{L}_\perp\) do not vanish, which means the total vector \(\vec{L}\) is inclined at an angle to \(\vec{\omega}\) and precesses around the axis. Thus, \(\vec{L}\) is not always parallel to \(\vec{\omega}\). Hence, the first statement is false.

Step 2: Conservation of Angular Momentum on a Swivel Chair
In the absence of an external torque acting about the vertical axis of rotation (\(\tau_{\text{ext}} = 0\)), the vertical component of angular momentum is strictly conserved: \[L_z = I \omega = \text{constant}\] When the person folds their arms inward towards the rotation axis, the perpendicular distances of the hand masses from the axis decrease. Consequently, the moment of inertia decreases: \[I_{\text{final}} < I_{\text{initial}}\] Since the product \(I \omega\) must remain invariant: \[\omega_{\text{final}} = \frac{I_{\text{initial}}}{I_{\text{final}}} \omega_{\text{initial}} > \omega_{\text{initial}}\] The rotational angular speed \(\omega\) increases accordingly. Hence, the second statement is true.

Step 3: Rotational Work-Energy Principle
The rotational kinetic energy of a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis with moment of inertia \(I\) is: \[K_{\text{rot}} = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2\] Differentiating this energy with respect to time \(t\): \[\frac{d K_{\text{rot}}}{dt} = \frac{1}{2} I \left(2\omega \frac{d\omega}{dt}\right) = I \alpha \omega\] According to the equation of rotational dynamics about a fixed axis, \(\tau_{\text{ext}} = I \alpha\). Substituting this relation yields: \[\frac{d K_{\text{rot}}}{dt} = \tau_{\text{ext}} \omega\] Since instantaneous rotational power is defined by \(P = \tau_{\text{ext}} \omega\), we have: \[P = \frac{d K_{\text{rot}}}{dt}\] The power delivered by the net torque is precisely equal to the time rate of change of rotational kinetic energy. Hence, the third statement is true.

Step 4: Check and Conclusion
The first statement is false, whereas the second statement and the third statement are true.
Final Conceptual Answer: Statement II and Statement III only.

हिंदी हल:

चरण 1: कोणीय संवेग और कोणीय वेग का संरेखण
स्थिर अक्ष के परितः घूर्णन कर रहे दृढ़ पिंड का कुल कोणीय संवेग: \[\vec{L} = \sum m_i (\vec{r}_i \times \vec{v}_i)\] घूर्णन अक्ष \(z\) के अनुदिश घटक \(L_z = I_z \omega\) होता है, किंतु यदि अक्ष पिंड की सममिति अक्ष न हो, तो अक्ष के लंबवत घटक \(L_x\) तथा \(L_y\) शून्य नहीं होते। ऐसी स्थिति में कुल कोणीय संवेग \(\vec{L}\) कोणीय वेग \(\vec{\omega}\) के समानांतर नहीं होता। अतः, प्रथम कथन असत्य है।

चरण 2: घूमने वाली कुर्सी पर कोणीय संवेग संरक्षण
घूर्णन अक्ष के परितः किसी बाह्य बल आघूर्ण की अनुपस्थिति में (\(\tau_{\text{ext}} = 0\)), कुल कोणीय संवेग संरक्षित रहता है: \[L = I \omega = \text{नियत}\] जब व्यक्ति अपनी भुजाओं को भीतर सिकोड़ता है, तो घूर्णन अक्ष से द्रव्यमान की दूरी घटने के कारण उसका जड़त्व आघूर्ण \(I\) घट जाता है। कोणीय संवेग नियत रहने के कारण उसकी कोणीय चाल \(\omega\) बढ़ जाती है। अतः, द्वितीय कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: घूर्णी कार्य-ऊर्जा प्रमेय तथा शक्ति
स्थिर अक्ष के परितः घूर्णी गतिज ऊर्जा निम्न है: \[K_{\text{rot}} = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2\] समय के सापेक्ष अवकलन करने पर: \[\frac{d K_{\text{rot}}}{dt} = I \omega \frac{d\omega}{dt} = (I \alpha) \omega = \tau_{\text{ext}} \omega\] चूँकि बल आघूर्ण द्वारा दी गई तात्कालिक शक्ति \(P = \tau_{\text{ext}} \omega\) होती है, अतः: \[P = \frac{d K_{\text{rot}}}{dt}\] अतः बाह्य बल आघूर्ण द्वारा आपूर्ति की गई शक्ति घूर्णी गतिज ऊर्जा के परिवर्तन की दर के बराबर होती है। अतः, तृतीय कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
प्रथम कथन असत्य है, जबकि द्वितीय कथन और तृतीय कथन सत्य हैं।
अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: केवल कथन II और कथन III।

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH06_MATCH_LIST_Q01 - Moments of inertia of symmetrical bodies

questiontext.text:
Match the physical body and axis of rotation in List-I with its corresponding moment of inertia in List-II (where \(M\) is mass, \(R\) is radius, and \(L\) is length):

List-I (Body and Axis) List-II (Moment of Inertia)
(A) Thin circular ring of radius \(R\) about central perpendicular axis (I) \(\frac{1}{12}ML^2\)
(B) Circular disc of radius \(R\) about its diameter (II) \(MR^2\)
(C) Thin uniform rod of length \(L\) about perpendicular axis through midpoint (III) \(\frac{2}{5}MR^2\)
(D) Uniform solid sphere of radius \(R\) about its diameter (IV) \(\frac{1}{4}MR^2\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of thin circular ring about central perpendicular axis
For a thin circular ring of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\), all mass elements are situated at a constant perpendicular distance \(R\) from the axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the ring plane. Integrating over all mass elements gives \(I = \sum m_i r_i^2 = MR^2\). This matches with Roman numeral II.

Step 2: Evaluation of circular disc about its diameter
For a uniform circular disc of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\), the moment of inertia about the central perpendicular axis is \(I_z = \frac{1}{2}MR^2\). By the perpendicular axes theorem for a planar laminar body, \(I_x + I_y = I_z\). Due to circular symmetry about any coplanar diameter, \(I_x = I_y = I_d\). Therefore, \(2I_d = \frac{1}{2}MR^2\), which yields \(I_d = \frac{1}{4}MR^2\). This matches with Roman numeral IV.

Step 3: Evaluation of thin uniform rod about perpendicular axis through midpoint
For a thin uniform rod of mass \(M\) and length \(L\), taking the origin at the centre gives linear mass density \(\lambda = \frac{M}{L}\). Integrating \(\mathrm{d}I = x^2\,\mathrm{d}m = \lambda x^2\,\mathrm{d}x\) from \(x = -L/2\) to \(x = +L/2\) yields \(I = \frac{M}{L}\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-L/2}^{L/2} = \frac{1}{12}ML^2\). This matches with Roman numeral I.

Step 4: Evaluation of uniform solid sphere about its diameter
For a uniform solid sphere of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\), integrating coaxial thin elemental discs along the diameter yields the standard moment of inertia \(I = \frac{2}{5}MR^2\). This matches with Roman numeral III.

Step 5: Check and Final Conclusion
Combining each matched pair consistently gives the overall matching: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH06_MATCH_LIST_Q02 - Translational and rotational kinematic dynamic analogues

questiontext.text:
Match each translational physical quantity in List-I with its corresponding rotational analogue in List-II:

List-I (Translational Quantity) List-II (Rotational Analogue)
(A) Linear momentum (\(\mathbf{p}\)) (I) Moment of inertia (\(I\))
(B) Force (\(\mathbf{F}\)) (II) Angular momentum (\(\mathbf{L}\))
(C) Linear mass (\(M\)) (III) Angular velocity (\(\boldsymbol{\omega}\))
(D) Linear velocity (\(\mathbf{v}\)) (IV) Torque (\(\boldsymbol{\tau}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analogue of linear momentum
Linear momentum is defined as \(\mathbf{p} = M\mathbf{v}\) and represents the quantity of translational motion. Its rotational counterpart represents the moment of momentum about a reference point or axis, defined as angular momentum \(\mathbf{L} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} = I\boldsymbol{\omega}\). This matches with Roman numeral II.

Step 2: Analogue of force
Force represents the rate of change of linear momentum in translational dynamics, \(\mathbf{F} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{p}}{\mathrm{d}t}\). The rotational analogue causing angular acceleration and governing the rate of change of angular momentum is torque, \(\boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{L}}{\mathrm{d}t}\). This matches with Roman numeral IV.

Step 3: Analogue of mass
Mass \(M\) is the measure of inertia in translational motion, resisting changes in linear velocity. In rotational motion about a fixed axis, the measure of rotational inertia resisting changes in angular velocity is the moment of inertia \(I = \sum m_i r_i^2\). This matches with Roman numeral I.

Step 4: Analogue of linear velocity
Linear velocity is the time rate of change of linear displacement, \(\mathbf{v} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{r}}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Its rotational counterpart, describing the time rate of angular displacement, is angular velocity \(\boldsymbol{\omega} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\theta}}{\mathrm{d}t}\). This matches with Roman numeral III.

Step 5: Check and Final Conclusion
Combining each matched pair consistently gives the overall matching: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH06_MATCH_LIST_Q03 - Dimensions of rotational physical quantities

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities related to rotational motion in List-I with their dimensional formulae in List-II:

List-I (Physical Quantity) List-II (Dimensional Formula)
(A) Angular momentum (I) \([\mathrm{M\,L^2}]\)
(B) Torque (II) \([\mathrm{M\,L^2\,T^{-2}}]\)
(C) Moment of inertia (III) \([\mathrm{T^{-2}}]\)
(D) Angular acceleration (IV) \([\mathrm{M\,L^2\,T^{-1}}]\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Dimensional formula of angular momentum
Angular momentum is defined as \(\mathbf{L} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p}\). Dimensionally, \([L] = [\text{length}] \times [\text{momentum}] = [\mathrm{L}] \times [\mathrm{M\,L\,T^{-1}}] = [\mathrm{M\,L^2\,T^{-1}}]\). This matches with Roman numeral IV.

Step 2: Dimensional formula of torque
Torque is defined as \(\boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F}\). Dimensionally, \([\tau] = [\text{length}] \times [\text{force}] = [\mathrm{L}] \times [\mathrm{M\,L\,T^{-2}}] = [\mathrm{M\,L^2\,T^{-2}}]\). This matches with Roman numeral II.

Step 3: Dimensional formula of moment of inertia
Moment of inertia is defined as \(I = \sum m_i r_i^2\). Dimensionally, \([I] = [\text{mass}] \times [\text{length}]^2 = [\mathrm{M\,L^2}]\). This matches with Roman numeral I.

Step 4: Dimensional formula of angular acceleration
Angular acceleration is defined as \(\boldsymbol{\alpha} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega}}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Since angular displacement is dimensionless, angular velocity has dimensions \([\mathrm{T^{-1}}]\), and angular acceleration has dimensions \(\frac{[\mathrm{T^{-1}}]}{[\mathrm{T}]} = [\mathrm{T^{-2}}]\) (or \([\mathrm{M^0\,L^0\,T^{-2}}]\)). This matches with Roman numeral III.

Step 5: Check and Final Conclusion
Combining each matched pair consistently gives the overall matching: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH06_MATCH_LIST_Q04 - Locations of centre of mass of bodies

questiontext.text:
Match the physical system described in List-I with the location of its centre of mass in List-II:

List-I (Physical System) List-II (Location of Centre of Mass)
(A) Three equal point masses placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side \(a\) (I) Distance \(\frac{L}{2}\) from either end
(B) Uniform thin rod of length \(L\) (II) At the centroid, at distance \(\frac{a}{\sqrt{3}}\) from each vertex
(C) Uniform circular ring of radius \(R\) (III) On the median, at distance \(\frac{h}{3}\) from the base
(D) Uniform triangular lamina of height \(h\) (IV) At the geometric centre, where no material is present

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of three equal point masses at vertices of equilateral triangle
Let the three identical masses \(m\) be placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side \(a\). By symmetry, the centre of mass lies at the centroid of the triangle. The distance from any vertex to the centroid along the median of length \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}a\) is given by \(\frac{2}{3} \times \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}a\right) = \frac{a}{\sqrt{3}}\). This matches with Roman numeral II.

Step 2: Evaluation of uniform thin rod of length \(L\)
For a uniform thin straight rod of mass \(M\) and length \(L\), linear mass density is constant. Integrating \(X_{\mathrm{cm}} = \frac{1}{M}\int_0^L x\,\lambda\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{1}{L}\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^L = \frac{L}{2}\). Thus, the centre of mass lies at the geometric midpoint, at a distance \(\frac{L}{2}\) from either end. This matches with Roman numeral I.

Step 3: Evaluation of uniform circular ring of radius \(R\)
By circular symmetry about any diameter, the centre of mass of a uniform thin circular ring lies at its geometric centre. Because the ring consists of matter only along its circumference, the geometric centre lies in the empty space enclosed by the ring where no material is present. This matches with Roman numeral IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of uniform triangular lamina of height \(h\)
A uniform triangular lamina can be considered as a collection of thin strips parallel to its base. The centre of mass of each strip lies at its midpoint, so the centre of mass of the whole lamina lies along the median connecting the vertex to the base midpoint. Integrating strips along the altitude from the base gives the centroid at a vertical distance of \(\frac{h}{3}\) from the base. This matches with Roman numeral III.

Step 5: Check and Final Conclusion
Combining each matched pair consistently gives the overall matching: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Center of mass of two point masses

questiontext.text: Two point masses of \(3\text{ kg}\) and \(5\text{ kg}\) are placed along the \(x\)-axis at \(x = 0\text{ m}\) and \(x = 16\text{ m}\), respectively. Calculate the distance of the centre of mass of the two-particle system from the \(3\text{ kg}\) mass (in \(\text{m}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of first particle: \(m_1 = 3\text{ kg}\) at position \(x_1 = 0\text{ m}\).
Mass of second particle: \(m_2 = 5\text{ kg}\) at position \(x_2 = 16\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The position of the centre of mass for a two-particle system along the \(x\)-axis is given by: \[ X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m_1 x_1 + m_2 x_2}{m_1 + m_2} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the given values into the formula: \[ X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{(3\text{ kg})(0\text{ m}) + (5\text{ kg})(16\text{ m})}{3\text{ kg} + 5\text{ kg}} \] \[ X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{0 + 80}{8} = 10\text{ m} \] Since the \(3\text{ kg}\) mass is located at the origin \(x = 0\text{ m}\), the distance of the centre of mass from the \(3\text{ kg}\) mass is \(10\text{ m}\).

Step 4: Check and Verification
The centre of mass must lie closer to the heavier mass. Here, the distance to the \(3\text{ kg}\) mass is \(10\text{ m}\) and the distance to the \(5\text{ kg}\) mass is \(6\text{ m}\), satisfying \(m_1 d_1 = 3 \times 10 = 30 = 5 \times 6 = m_2 d_2\).

Final Answer: The distance of the centre of mass from the \(3\text{ kg}\) mass is \(10\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Linear speed from angular velocity

questiontext.text: A wheel rotates about a fixed axis with a constant angular speed of \(6.0\text{ rad/s}\). Find the linear speed of a point located at a perpendicular distance of \(0.50\text{ m}\) from the axis of rotation (in \(\text{m/s}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Angular velocity of rotation: \(\omega = 6.0\text{ rad/s}\).
Perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation: \(r = 0.50\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
For a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis, the linear speed \(v\) of any particle at perpendicular distance \(r\) is related to angular speed \(\omega\) by: \[ v = \omega r \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the given numerical quantities: \[ v = (6.0\text{ rad/s}) \times (0.50\text{ m}) = 3.0\text{ m/s} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Units check: \(\text{rad/s} \times \text{m} = \text{m/s}\). The result is physically reasonable for a point on a rotating wheel.

Final Answer: The linear speed of the point is \(3\text{ m/s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Scalar product of two vectors

questiontext.text: Given two vectors \(\mathbf{a} = 2\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3\hat{\mathbf{j}}\) and \(\mathbf{b} = 4\hat{\mathbf{i}} - \hat{\mathbf{j}}\), calculate their scalar (dot) product \(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Vector \(\mathbf{a} = 2\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3\hat{\mathbf{j}} + 0\hat{\mathbf{k}}\).
Vector \(\mathbf{b} = 4\hat{\mathbf{i}} - 1\hat{\mathbf{j}} + 0\hat{\mathbf{k}}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The scalar product of two vectors in component form is: \[ \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = a_x b_x + a_y b_y + a_z b_z \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Multiply corresponding components: \[ a_x b_x = 2 \times 4 = 8 \] \[ a_y b_y = 3 \times (-1) = -3 \] \[ a_z b_z = 0 \times 0 = 0 \] Sum the component products: \[ \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = 8 + (-3) + 0 = 5 \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Both vectors lie in the \(xy\)-plane. The scalar product is positive, indicating an acute angle between them.

Final Answer: The scalar product \(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}\) is \(5\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Mechanical advantage of ideal lever

questiontext.text: In an ideal lever, the load arm is \(0.25\text{ m}\) and the effort arm is \(1.0\text{ m}\). Calculate the mechanical advantage of the lever.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Load arm: \(d_1 = 0.25\text{ m}\).
Effort arm: \(d_2 = 1.0\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
By the principle of moments for an ideal lever in rotational equilibrium: \[ \text{Load} \times \text{Load arm} = \text{Effort} \times \text{Effort arm} \] The mechanical advantage (MA) is defined as the ratio of load to effort, or the ratio of effort arm to load arm: \[ \text{MA} = \frac{d_2}{d_1} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the lengths into the expression: \[ \text{MA} = \frac{1.0\text{ m}}{0.25\text{ m}} = 4.0 \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Since the effort arm is greater than the load arm, the mechanical advantage is greater than \(1\), which is correct for a lever designed to amplify force.

Final Answer: The mechanical advantage of the lever is \(4\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Moment of inertia of circular ring

questiontext.text: A uniform thin circular ring has a mass of \(4.0\text{ kg}\) and a radius of \(0.50\text{ m}\). Calculate its moment of inertia about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane (in \(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of the ring: \(M = 4.0\text{ kg}\).
Radius of the ring: \(R = 0.50\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The moment of inertia of a uniform thin circular ring of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\) about its central axis perpendicular to the plane of the ring is: \[ I = M R^2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the values into the formula: \[ I = (4.0\text{ kg}) \times (0.50\text{ m})^2 = 4.0 \times 0.25 = 1.0\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2 \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
All mass elements of the thin ring are at the exact same distance \(R\) from the central axis, confirming \(I = \sum m_i r_i^2 = M R^2\).

Final Answer: The moment of inertia of the ring is \(1\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Torque of perpendicular applied force

questiontext.text: A force of magnitude \(25\text{ N}\) acts perpendicularly on a door at a distance of \(0.40\text{ m}\) from the hinge line. Calculate the magnitude of torque exerted by this force about the hinge axis (in \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Applied force magnitude: \(F = 25\text{ N}\).
Distance from hinge axis: \(r = 0.40\text{ m}\).
Angle between position vector and force vector: \(\theta = 90^\circ\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The magnitude of torque \(\tau\) is given by: \[ \tau = r F \sin\theta \] Since the force is applied perpendicularly, \(\sin 90^\circ = 1\), simplifying to: \[ \tau = r F \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the given values: \[ \tau = (0.40\text{ m}) \times (25\text{ N}) = 10\text{ N}\cdot\text{m} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Dimensional consistency: force in newtons multiplied by distance in metres yields torque in \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\).

Final Answer: The magnitude of the torque is \(10\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Rotational kinetic energy of rotating body

questiontext.text: A rigid body having a moment of inertia of \(0.80\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\) rotates about a fixed axis with a constant angular speed of \(5.0\text{ rad/s}\). Find its rotational kinetic energy (in \(\text{J}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Moment of inertia: \(I = 0.80\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\).
Angular velocity: \(\omega = 5.0\text{ rad/s}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The rotational kinetic energy \(K\) of a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis is: \[ K = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the given values: \[ K = \frac{1}{2} \times (0.80\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2) \times (5.0\text{ rad/s})^2 \] \[ K = 0.40 \times 25 = 10\text{ J} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Units check: \(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2 \cdot \text{s}^{-2} = \text{N}\cdot\text{m} = \text{J}\). The result is non-negative and quantitatively consistent.

Final Answer: The rotational kinetic energy of the body is \(10\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Center of mass of three particles on triangle

questiontext.text: Three particles of masses \(1.0\text{ kg}\), \(2.0\text{ kg}\), and \(3.0\text{ kg}\) are situated at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side length \(1.8\text{ m}\). If the \(1.0\text{ kg}\) mass is at the origin \((0,0)\) and the \(2.0\text{ kg}\) mass lies along the positive \(x\)-axis at \((1.8\text{ m}, 0)\), find the \(x\)-coordinate of the centre of mass of the system (in \(\text{m}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass \(m_1 = 1.0\text{ kg}\) at coordinates \((x_1, y_1) = (0, 0)\).
Mass \(m_2 = 2.0\text{ kg}\) at coordinates \((x_2, y_2) = (1.8\text{ m}, 0)\).
Mass \(m_3 = 3.0\text{ kg}\) at the third vertex of the equilateral triangle, where \(x_3 = 1.8 / 2 = 0.9\text{ m}\) and \(y_3 = 1.8 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 0.9\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The \(x\)-coordinate of the centre of mass is given by: \[ X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m_1 x_1 + m_2 x_2 + m_3 x_3}{m_1 + m_2 + m_3} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Calculate total mass of the system: \[ M = 1.0\text{ kg} + 2.0\text{ kg} + 3.0\text{ kg} = 6.0\text{ kg} \] Calculate the numerator: \[ m_1 x_1 = 1.0 \times 0 = 0\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m} \] \[ m_2 x_2 = 2.0 \times 1.8 = 3.6\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m} \] \[ m_3 x_3 = 3.0 \times 0.9 = 2.7\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m} \] \[ \sum m_i x_i = 0 + 3.6 + 2.7 = 6.3\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m} \] Compute \(X_{\text{cm}}\): \[ X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{6.3\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}}{6.0\text{ kg}} = 1.05\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
The \(x\)-coordinate lies within the bounds \(0 < 1.05 < 1.8\text{ m}\), shifted toward the heavier masses \(m_2\) and \(m_3\) as expected physically.

Final Answer: The \(x\)-coordinate of the centre of mass is \(1.05\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Center of mass y coordinate of particles

questiontext.text: Three particles of equal mass \(2.0\text{ kg}\) each are placed at coordinates \((0, 0)\), \((2.0\text{ m}, 0)\), and \((1.0\text{ m}, 3.0\text{ m})\). Calculate the \(y\)-coordinate of the centre of mass of the system (in \(\text{m}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Masses: \(m_1 = m_2 = m_3 = 2.0\text{ kg}\).
Coordinates of particles: \((x_1, y_1) = (0, 0)\), \((x_2, y_2) = (2.0\text{ m}, 0)\), and \((x_3, y_3) = (1.0\text{ m}, 3.0\text{ m})\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The \(y\)-coordinate of the centre of mass is given by: \[ Y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m_1 y_1 + m_2 y_2 + m_3 y_3}{m_1 + m_2 + m_3} \] For equal masses, this simplifies to the arithmetic mean: \[ Y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{y_1 + y_2 + y_3}{3} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the \(y\)-coordinates: \[ Y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{0 + 0 + 3.0\text{ m}}{3} = \frac{3.0}{3} = 1.0\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Two masses lie at \(y = 0\) and one mass lies at \(y = 3.0\text{ m}\). The centroid of these three equal masses is at one-third of the altitude, which is exactly \(1.0\text{ m}\).

Final Answer: The \(y\)-coordinate of the centre of mass is \(1\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Center of mass of composite square lamina

questiontext.text: A uniform L-shaped lamina of total mass \(3.0\text{ kg}\) is formed by three identical square sections, each of side \(1.0\text{ m}\) and mass \(1.0\text{ kg}\). The centers of the three squares are located at \((0.5\text{ m}, 0.5\text{ m})\), \((1.5\text{ m}, 0.5\text{ m})\), and \((0.5\text{ m}, 1.5\text{ m})\). Find the \(x\)-coordinate of the centre of mass of the lamina (in \(\text{m}\), rounded to two decimal places).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The lamina consists of three identical squares: Square 1: Mass \(m_1 = 1.0\text{ kg}\), center at \((x_1, y_1) = (0.5\text{ m}, 0.5\text{ m})\).
Square 2: Mass \(m_2 = 1.0\text{ kg}\), center at \((x_2, y_2) = (1.5\text{ m}, 0.5\text{ m})\).
Square 3: Mass \(m_3 = 1.0\text{ kg}\), center at \((x_3, y_3) = (0.5\text{ m}, 1.5\text{ m})\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The centre of mass of a system of uniform components is: \[ X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\sum m_i x_i}{\sum m_i} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Calculate total mass: \[ M = 1.0 + 1.0 + 1.0 = 3.0\text{ kg} \] Compute the sum of moments of masses: \[ \sum m_i x_i = (1.0 \times 0.5) + (1.0 \times 1.5) + (1.0 \times 0.5) = 0.5 + 1.5 + 0.5 = 2.5\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m} \] Calculate \(X_{\text{cm}}\): \[ X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{2.5}{3.0} = \frac{5}{6}\text{ m} \approx 0.833\text{ m} \] Rounded to two decimal places, this is \(0.83\text{ m}\).

Step 4: Check and Verification
By symmetry between the \(x\) and \(y\) coordinates, \(Y_{\text{cm}} = X_{\text{cm}} = 5/6\text{ m}\), and the point lies along the diagonal line of symmetry of the L-shape.

Final Answer: The \(x\)-coordinate of the centre of mass is \(0.83\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Center of mass in diatomic molecule

questiontext.text: In a hydrogen chloride (\(\text{HCl}\)) molecule, the separation between the nuclei of the hydrogen and chlorine atoms is \(1.27\text{ \AA}\) (\(1.27 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\)). Given that a chlorine atom is approximately \(35.5\) times as massive as a hydrogen atom, calculate the distance of the centre of mass of the molecule from the hydrogen nucleus (in \(\text{\AA}\), rounded to two decimal places).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Separation between atoms: \(d = 1.27\text{ \AA}\).
Mass ratio: \(m_{\text{Cl}} = 35.5\, m_{\text{H}}\).
Take the origin at the hydrogen nucleus, so \(x_{\text{H}} = 0\) and \(x_{\text{Cl}} = 1.27\text{ \AA}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The position of the centre of mass from the hydrogen nucleus is: \[ x_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m_{\text{H}} x_{\text{H}} + m_{\text{Cl}} x_{\text{Cl}}}{m_{\text{H}} + m_{\text{Cl}}} \] Substituting \(x_{\text{H}} = 0\): \[ x_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m_{\text{Cl}} d}{m_{\text{H}} + m_{\text{Cl}}} = \frac{35.5\, m_{\text{H}} d}{m_{\text{H}} + 35.5\, m_{\text{H}}} = \frac{35.5}{36.5} d \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute \(d = 1.27\text{ \AA}\): \[ x_{\text{cm}} = \frac{35.5}{36.5} \times 1.27 = 0.9726 \times 1.27 \approx 1.2352\text{ \AA} \] Rounding to two decimal places gives \(1.24\text{ \AA}\).

Step 4: Check and Verification
The chlorine atom is much heavier than hydrogen, so the centre of mass must lie extremely close to the chlorine atom: \(1.27 - 1.24 = 0.03\text{ \AA}\) from chlorine, which matches physical intuition.

Final Answer: The distance of the centre of mass from the hydrogen nucleus is \(1.24\text{ \AA}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Acceleration of center of mass under forces

questiontext.text: A rigid system of total mass \(5.0\text{ kg}\) is subjected to two external forces: \(\mathbf{F}_1 = 12\hat{\mathbf{i}}\text{ N}\) and \(\mathbf{F}_2 = 16\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ N}\). Internal forces within the system cancel in pairs. Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of the centre of mass of the system (in \(\text{m/s}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total mass of the system: \(M = 5.0\text{ kg}\).
External forces: \(\mathbf{F}_1 = 12\hat{\mathbf{i}}\text{ N}\) and \(\mathbf{F}_2 = 16\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ N}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
Newton's second law for a system of particles states: \[ \mathbf{F}_{\text{ext}} = M \mathbf{a}_{\text{cm}} \] The net external force is: \[ \mathbf{F}_{\text{ext}} = \mathbf{F}_1 + \mathbf{F}_2 = 12\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 16\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ N} \] The magnitude of the net external force is: \[ |\mathbf{F}_{\text{ext}}| = \sqrt{F_x^2 + F_y^2} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Calculate the magnitude of \(\mathbf{F}_{\text{ext}}\): \[ |\mathbf{F}_{\text{ext}}| = \sqrt{12^2 + 16^2} = \sqrt{144 + 256} = \sqrt{400} = 20\text{ N} \] Compute the magnitude of acceleration: \[ a_{\text{cm}} = \frac{|\mathbf{F}_{\text{ext}}|}{M} = \frac{20\text{ N}}{5.0\text{ kg}} = 4.0\text{ m/s}^2 \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Units check: \(\text{N}/\text{kg} = \text{m/s}^2\). Only external forces accelerate the centre of mass; internal forces play no role in changing the momentum of the centre of mass.

Final Answer: The magnitude of acceleration of the centre of mass is \(4\text{ m/s}^2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Magnitude of vector product of vectors

questiontext.text: Given two vectors \(\mathbf{a} = 2\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 2\hat{\mathbf{j}} + \hat{\mathbf{k}}\) and \(\mathbf{b} = 2\hat{\mathbf{i}} - \hat{\mathbf{j}} - 2\hat{\mathbf{k}}\), calculate the magnitude of their vector (cross) product \(|\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}|\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Vectors: \(\mathbf{a} = 2\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 2\hat{\mathbf{j}} + \hat{\mathbf{k}}\) and \(\mathbf{b} = 2\hat{\mathbf{i}} - \hat{\mathbf{j}} - 2\hat{\mathbf{k}}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The vector product \(\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}\) is evaluated using the determinant: \[ \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ a_x & a_y & a_z \\ b_x & b_y & b_z \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{i}}(a_y b_z - a_z b_y) - \hat{\mathbf{j}}(a_x b_z - a_z b_x) + \hat{\mathbf{k}}(a_x b_y - a_y b_x) \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Calculate individual components: \[ (\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b})_x = (2)(-2) - (1)(-1) = -4 + 1 = -3 \] \[ (\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b})_y = -\left[(2)(-2) - (1)(2)\right] = -[-4 - 2] = 6 \] \[ (\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b})_z = (2)(-1) - (2)(2) = -2 - 4 = -6 \] Thus: \[ \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = -3\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 6\hat{\mathbf{j}} - 6\hat{\mathbf{k}} \] Now compute the magnitude: \[ |\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}| = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + 6^2 + (-6)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 36 + 36} = \sqrt{81} = 9 \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Notice that \(|\mathbf{a}| = \sqrt{4+4+1} = 3\) and \(|\mathbf{b}| = \sqrt{4+1+4} = 3\). Their dot product is \(\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = 4 - 2 - 2 = 0\), meaning they are orthogonal. Hence \(|\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}| = |\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}| \sin 90^\circ = 3 \times 3 \times 1 = 9\).

Final Answer: The magnitude of the vector product is \(9\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Linear velocity from cross product

questiontext.text: A rigid body is rotating about the \(z\)-axis with an angular velocity \(\boldsymbol{\omega} = 3\hat{\mathbf{k}}\text{ rad/s}\). Find the magnitude of the linear velocity of a particle located at position vector \(\mathbf{r} = 4\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ m}\) (in \(\text{m/s}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Angular velocity vector: \(\boldsymbol{\omega} = 3\hat{\mathbf{k}}\text{ rad/s}\).
Position vector: \(\mathbf{r} = 4\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
Linear velocity \(\mathbf{v}\) is related to angular velocity \(\boldsymbol{\omega}\) and position vector \(\mathbf{r}\) by: \[ \mathbf{v} = \boldsymbol{\omega} \times \mathbf{r} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Evaluate the vector cross product: \[ \mathbf{v} = (3\hat{\mathbf{k}}) \times (4\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3\hat{\mathbf{j}}) \] Using unit vector identities \(\hat{\mathbf{k}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}} = \hat{\mathbf{j}}\) and \(\hat{\mathbf{k}} \times \hat{\mathbf{j}} = -\hat{\mathbf{i}}\): \[ \mathbf{v} = 12\hat{\mathbf{j}} + 9(-\\hat{\mathbf{i}}) = -9\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 12\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ m/s} \] Compute the magnitude: \[ |\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{(-9)^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{81 + 144} = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ m/s} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
The perpendicular distance from the \(z\)-axis is \(r_\perp = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5\text{ m}\). Since \(\mathbf{v}\) lies in the \(xy\)-plane, its speed is \(v = \omega r_\perp = 3 \times 5 = 15\text{ m/s}\).

Final Answer: The magnitude of the linear velocity is \(15\text{ m/s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Magnitude of torque vector about origin

questiontext.text: A force \(\mathbf{F} = 4\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 5\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ N}\) acts on a particle whose position vector with respect to the origin is \(\mathbf{r} = 3\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 2\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ m}\). Calculate the magnitude of the torque exerted by this force about the origin (in \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Position vector: \(\mathbf{r} = 3\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 2\hat{\mathbf{j}} + 0\hat{\mathbf{k}}\text{ m}\).
Force vector: \(\mathbf{F} = 4\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 5\hat{\mathbf{j}} + 0\hat{\mathbf{k}}\text{ N}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The torque vector about the origin is defined as: \[ \boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F} \] For vectors in the \(xy\)-plane, the torque is directed along the \(z\)-axis: \[ \boldsymbol{\tau} = (x F_y - y F_x)\hat{\mathbf{k}} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the component values: \[ x F_y = (3\text{ m}) \times (5\text{ N}) = 15\text{ N}\cdot\text{m} \] \[ y F_x = (2\text{ m}) \times (4\text{ N}) = 8\text{ N}\cdot\text{m} \] Subtract: \[ \tau_z = 15 - 8 = 7\text{ N}\cdot\text{m} \] Thus: \[ \boldsymbol{\tau} = 7\hat{\mathbf{k}}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m} \] The magnitude is: \[ |\boldsymbol{\tau}| = 7\text{ N}\cdot\text{m} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Both vectors lie in the \(xy\)-plane, so the torque points along \(\hat{\mathbf{k}}\). The positive sign indicates a counterclockwise rotational tendency.

Final Answer: The magnitude of the torque about the origin is \(7\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Angular momentum of straight line particle

questiontext.text: A particle of mass \(2.0\text{ kg}\) moves with a uniform velocity of \(5.0\text{ m/s}\) parallel to the \(x\)-axis along the straight line \(y = 4.0\text{ m}\). Calculate the magnitude of its angular momentum about the origin (in \(\text{J}\cdot\text{s}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of particle: \(m = 2.0\text{ kg}\).
Velocity: \(\mathbf{v} = 5.0\hat{\mathbf{i}}\text{ m/s}\).
Line of motion: \(y = 4.0\text{ m}\), parallel to the \(x\)-axis.

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The angular momentum about the origin is: \[ \mathbf{l} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} = \mathbf{r} \times (m\mathbf{v}) \] The magnitude of angular momentum is given by: \[ l = p \cdot r_\perp = m v r_\perp \] where \(r_\perp\) is the perpendicular distance from the origin to the line of motion.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Identify \(r_\perp\): \[ r_\perp = 4.0\text{ m} \] Substitute the values into the formula: \[ l = (2.0\text{ kg}) \times (5.0\text{ m/s}) \times (4.0\text{ m}) \] \[ l = 10.0 \times 4.0 = 40.0\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s} = 40\text{ J}\cdot\text{s} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Since the motion is along a straight line at constant velocity, the perpendicular distance from the origin remains constant throughout, verifying that the angular momentum about the origin is conserved and constant.

Final Answer: The magnitude of the angular momentum is \(40\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Effort force required in balanced lever

questiontext.text: A lever of negligible mass is balanced horizontally on a fulcrum. A load of \(600\text{ N}\) is placed on one side at a distance of \(0.20\text{ m}\) from the fulcrum. Calculate the effort force required to balance the load if it is applied at a distance of \(1.20\text{ m}\) on the other side of the fulcrum (in \(\text{N}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Load force: \(F_1 = 600\text{ N}\).
Load arm: \(d_1 = 0.20\text{ m}\).
Effort arm: \(d_2 = 1.20\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
For rotational equilibrium about the fulcrum, the sum of clockwise and counterclockwise torques must be zero: \[ F_1 d_1 = F_2 d_2 \] where \(F_2\) is the applied effort.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Rearrange for the effort \(F_2\): \[ F_2 = \frac{F_1 d_1}{d_2} \] Substitute the values: \[ F_2 = \frac{(600\text{ N}) \times (0.20\text{ m})}{1.20\text{ m}} = \frac{120}{1.20} = 100\text{ N} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
The mechanical advantage is \(d_2 / d_1 = 1.20 / 0.20 = 6\). The effort required is \(600 / 6 = 100\text{ N}\), confirming the result.

Final Answer: The effort force required is \(100\text{ N}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Moment of inertia of circular disc

questiontext.text: A uniform circular disc of mass \(4.0\text{ kg}\) has a radius of \(0.60\text{ m}\). Calculate the moment of inertia of the disc about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane (in \(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of the disc: \(M = 4.0\text{ kg}\).
Radius of the disc: \(R = 0.60\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The moment of inertia of a uniform circular disc of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\) about its central perpendicular axis is: \[ I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the given values: \[ I = \frac{1}{2} \times (4.0\text{ kg}) \times (0.60\text{ m})^2 \] \[ I = 2.0 \times 0.36 = 0.72\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2 \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Comparing with a ring of the same mass and radius (\(I = 1.44\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\)), the disc has half the moment of inertia because its mass is distributed continuously from the centre to the rim.

Final Answer: The moment of inertia of the disc is \(0.72\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q19 - Moment of inertia of solid sphere

questiontext.text: Calculate the moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of mass \(5.0\text{ kg}\) and radius \(0.40\text{ m}\) about an axis passing through its diameter (in \(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of the solid sphere: \(M = 5.0\text{ kg}\).
Radius of the solid sphere: \(R = 0.40\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere about any diameter is given by: \[ I = \frac{2}{5} M R^2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the given values: \[ I = \frac{2}{5} \times (5.0\text{ kg}) \times (0.40\text{ m})^2 \] \[ I = 2.0 \times 0.16 = 0.32\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2 \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Units check: \(\text{kg} \times \text{m}^2 = \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\). For a spherical shell, the coefficient is \(2/3\), which is greater than \(2/5\)} for a solid sphere because more mass is concentrated farther from the axis.

Final Answer: The moment of inertia of the solid sphere is \(0.32\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q20 - Radius of gyration of uniform thin rod

questiontext.text: A uniform thin rod of length \(L = 2\sqrt{3}\text{ m} \approx 3.464\text{ m}\) rotates about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through its midpoint. Calculate the radius of gyration of the rod about this axis (in \(\text{m}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of the rod: \(L = 2\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\).
Axis location: Perpendicular to the rod, passing through its centre of mass.

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod of length \(L\) and mass \(M\) about a central perpendicular axis is: \[ I = \frac{M L^2}{12} \] The radius of gyration \(k\) is related to moment of inertia by: \[ I = M k^2 \implies k = \sqrt{\frac{I}{M}} = \frac{L}{\sqrt{12}} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Simplify \(\sqrt{12}\): \[ \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3} \] Substitute \(L = 2\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\): \[ k = \frac{2\sqrt{3}\text{ m}}{2\sqrt{3}} = 1.0\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
The radius of gyration must be less than half the rod length (\(L/2 = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.732\text{ m}\)). Since \(1.0 < 1.732\), the result is physically consistent.

Final Answer: The radius of gyration of the rod is \(1\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q21 - Angular speed from constant angular acceleration

questiontext.text: A flywheel starting from rest accelerates uniformly with an angular acceleration of \(3.0\text{ rad/s}^2\). Determine its angular speed after \(8.0\text{ s}\) (in \(\text{rad/s}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial angular speed: \(\omega_0 = 0\text{ rad/s}\).
Angular acceleration: \(\alpha = 3.0\text{ rad/s}^2\).
Time interval: \(t = 8.0\text{ s}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The rotational kinematic equation for uniform angular acceleration is: \[ \omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the given values: \[ \omega = 0 + (3.0\text{ rad/s}^2) \times (8.0\text{ s}) = 24.0\text{ rad/s} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Dimensional check: \(\text{rad/s}^2 \times \text{s} = \text{rad/s}\). The speed increases linearly with time under constant acceleration.

Final Answer: The angular speed after \(8.0\text{ s}\) is \(24\text{ rad/s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q22 - Angular displacement during uniform angular acceleration

questiontext.text: A body starts from rest and undergoes uniform rotational acceleration of \(3.0\text{ rad/s}^2\). Find its total angular displacement after \(8.0\text{ s}\) (in \(\text{rad}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial angular speed: \(\omega_0 = 0\text{ rad/s}\).
Angular acceleration: \(\alpha = 3.0\text{ rad/s}^2\).
Time elapsed: \(t = 8.0\text{ s}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The rotational kinematic relation for angular displacement \(\theta\) is: \[ \theta = \omega_0 t + \frac{1}{2} \alpha t^2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the given values: \[ \theta = 0 + \frac{1}{2} \times (3.0\text{ rad/s}^2) \times (8.0\text{ s})^2 \] \[ \theta = 1.5 \times 64 = 96.0\text{ rad} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Alternative check using average angular velocity: \(\omega_{\text{avg}} = (0 + 24)/2 = 12\text{ rad/s}\). Then \(\theta = \omega_{\text{avg}} \times t = 12 \times 8 = 96\text{ rad}\), confirming the result.

Final Answer: The angular displacement is \(96\text{ rad}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q23 - Angular retardation bringing wheel to rest

questiontext.text: A wheel rotating at \(1200\text{ rev/min}\) is brought to rest uniformly in \(20\text{ s}\). Find the magnitude of its angular retardation (in \(\text{rad/s}^2\), using \(\pi \approx 3.1416\), rounded to two decimal places).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial angular speed: \(\nu_0 = 1200\text{ rev/min}\).
Final angular speed: \(\omega = 0\text{ rad/s}\).
Time taken: \(t = 20\text{ s}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
Convert initial angular speed to \(\text{rad/s}\): \[ \omega_0 = 2\pi \nu_0 = \frac{2\pi \times 1200}{60} = 40\pi\text{ rad/s} \] Using rotational kinematic relation: \[ \omega = \omega_0 - \alpha t \implies \alpha = \frac{\omega_0 - \omega}{t} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the values: \[ \alpha = \frac{40\pi - 0}{20} = 2\pi\text{ rad/s}^2 \] Using \(\pi \approx 3.1416\): \[ \alpha = 2 \times 3.1416 = 6.2832\text{ rad/s}^2 \approx 6.28\text{ rad/s}^2 \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
In \(20\text{ s}\), an angular retardation of \(2\pi\text{ rad/s}^2\) reduces the angular velocity from \(40\pi\text{ rad/s}\) to \(0\), which is exact.

Final Answer: The magnitude of the angular retardation is \(6.28\text{ rad/s}^2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q24 - Angular acceleration from applied torque

questiontext.text: A constant torque of \(50\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\) is applied to a rotor having a moment of inertia of \(2.5\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\) about its fixed axis of rotation. Calculate the angular acceleration produced in the rotor (in \(\text{rad/s}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Applied torque: \(\tau = 50\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\).
Moment of inertia: \(I = 2.5\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
Newton's second law for rotation about a fixed axis is: \[ \tau = I \alpha \] where \(\alpha\) is the angular acceleration.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Rearrange for \(\alpha\): \[ \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{50\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}}{2.5\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2} = 20.0\text{ rad/s}^2 \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Units check: \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m} / (\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2) = (\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s}^2) / (\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2) = \text{s}^{-2} = \text{rad/s}^2\).

Final Answer: The angular acceleration produced is \(20\text{ rad/s}^2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q25 - Work done by constant rotational torque

questiontext.text: A constant torque of \(30\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\) acts on a wheel rotating about its fixed axis, turning it through an angular displacement of \(15\text{ rad}\). Calculate the work done by the torque on the wheel (in \(\text{J}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Constant torque: \(\tau = 30\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\).
Angular displacement: \(\Delta\theta = 15\text{ rad}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The work done by a constant torque during an angular displacement \(\Delta\theta\) is: \[ W = \tau \Delta\theta \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute the given values: \[ W = (30\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}) \times (15\text{ rad}) = 450\text{ J} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Units check: \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m} \times \text{rad} = \text{J}\). The work done is positive as the torque acts in the direction of the angular displacement.

Final Answer: The work done by the torque is \(450\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q26 - Rotational kinetic energy of solid cylinder

questiontext.text: A uniform solid cylinder of mass \(20.0\text{ kg}\) and radius \(0.25\text{ m}\) rotates about its symmetry axis with an angular speed of \(100.0\text{ rad/s}\). Calculate the rotational kinetic energy of the cylinder (in \(\text{J}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of the cylinder: \(M = 20.0\text{ kg}\).
Radius of the cylinder: \(R = 0.25\text{ m}\).
Angular velocity: \(\omega = 100.0\text{ rad/s}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The moment of inertia of a uniform solid cylinder of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\) about its central longitudinal axis is: \[ I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 \] The rotational kinetic energy is: \[ K = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Calculate the moment of inertia \(I\): \[ I = \frac{1}{2} \times (20.0\text{ kg}) \times (0.25\text{ m})^2 = 10.0 \times 0.0625 = 0.625\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2 \] Compute the rotational kinetic energy: \[ K = \frac{1}{2} \times (0.625\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2) \times (100.0\text{ rad/s})^2 \] \[ K = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.625 \times 10000 = 0.3125 \times 10000 = 3125\text{ J} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Units check: \(\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2 \cdot \text{s}^{-2} = \text{J}\). The result is fully consistent with standard rotational kinetic energy calculations.

Final Answer: The rotational kinetic energy of the cylinder is \(3125\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q27 - Angular momentum of rotating solid cylinder

questiontext.text: A uniform solid cylinder of mass \(20.0\text{ kg}\) and radius \(0.25\text{ m}\) rotates about its central symmetry axis with an angular speed of \(100.0\text{ rad/s}\). Calculate the magnitude of the angular momentum of the cylinder associated with its rotation about the axis (in \(\text{J}\cdot\text{s}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of the cylinder: \(M = 20.0\text{ kg}\).
Radius of the cylinder: \(R = 0.25\text{ m}\).
Angular velocity: \(\omega = 100.0\text{ rad/s}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
The moment of inertia of a uniform solid cylinder about its symmetry axis is: \[ I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 \] The magnitude of the angular momentum about the fixed axis of rotation is: \[ L = I \omega \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Calculate the moment of inertia \(I\): \[ I = \frac{1}{2} \times 20.0 \times (0.25)^2 = 10.0 \times 0.0625 = 0.625\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2 \] Calculate the angular momentum \(L\): \[ L = (0.625\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2) \times (100.0\text{ rad/s}) = 62.5\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s} = 62.5\text{ J}\cdot\text{s} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
Connecting with rotational kinetic energy: \(K = \frac{L^2}{2I} = \frac{(62.5)^2}{2 \times 0.625} = \frac{3906.25}{1.25} = 3125\text{ J}\), which exactly matches the energy calculated previously.

Final Answer: The magnitude of the angular momentum is \(62.5\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SYSTEMS_OF_PARTICLES_AND_ROTATIONAL_MOTION_NUMERICAL_Q28 - Final angular speed from conservation of angular momentum

questiontext.text: A child stands at the centre of a turntable with his two arms outstretched. The turntable is set rotating with an initial angular speed of \(40\text{ rev/min}\). When the child folds his hands back, the moment of inertia of the system decreases to \(\frac{2}{5}\) of its initial value. Calculate the new angular speed of the turntable (in \(\text{rev/min}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial angular speed: \(\omega_1 = 40\text{ rev/min}\).
Initial moment of inertia: \(I_1\).
Final moment of inertia: \(I_2 = \frac{2}{5} I_1 = 0.4 I_1\).
No external torque acts on the turntable system.

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
In the absence of external torque (\(\tau_{\text{ext}} = 0\)), the total angular momentum of the system is conserved: \[ L_1 = L_2 \implies I_1 \omega_1 = I_2 \omega_2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Substitute \(I_2 = \frac{2}{5} I_1\) into the conservation relation: \[ I_1 \omega_1 = \left(\frac{2}{5} I_1\right) \omega_2 \] Cancel \(I_1\) from both sides: \[ \omega_2 = \frac{5}{2} \omega_1 \] Substitute \(\omega_1 = 40\text{ rev/min}\): \[ \omega_2 = 2.5 \times 40 = 100\text{ rev/min} \]

Step 4: Check and Verification
